custominfo-commands:
Host commands
Only the world host (administrator) can use these commands

RaftModLoader console (F10)
Enter commands without a leading /
Player name is optional - when omitted, the command targets the host
Editing other players is not supported yet because network syncing has not been implemented

Skill levels
level add [player] [skill] [levels] - add levels
level set [player] [skill] [level] - set level
level get [player] [skill] - show level
level reset [player] [skill] - reset skill

Experience
exp add [player] [skill] [experience] - add XP
exp set [player] [skill] [experience] - set XP
exp get [player] [skill] - show XP

Ability tiers
tier add [player] [skill] [ability] [tiers] - add tiers
tier set [player] [skill] [ability] [tier] - set tier
tier get [player] [skill] [ability] - show tier

Unlearn points
unlearnpoints add [amount] - add points
unlearnpoints set [amount] - set points
unlearnpoints get - show points

Examples
exp add survival 100
level set cooking 10
tier set sailing steadyhelm 2
unlearnpoints add 5

custominfo-details-5:
How weather works
Air temperature depends on time of day, current weather and climate periods. Heatwaves, cool, dry and humid periods, and sultry nights affect temperature and humidity. Rain cools the air. Direct sun increases heat stress; shade reduces it.

Body temperature
Normal body temperature is about 36.6 °C. Heat, sunlight, humidity, cool air, rain, getting wet, immersion in water and nearby burning heat sources all matter. Being wet speeds up heat loss in the cold, while high humidity makes evaporative cooling less effective.

Hypothermia
By default, below 35 °C, movement gradually slows. At 31 °C, walking and swimming speed fall to 60% of normal. Frost appears at the screen edges. By default, at or below 33 °C, the player takes damage every 2 seconds by default, increasing as body temperature falls. Water and cold rain speed cooling; shelter and fire help you warm up.

Overheating
By default, at 38 °C, extra thirst loss begins and the heat-screen effect appears. Movement speed gradually decreases by up to 10% at 41 °C. Nausea and wave-like screen distortion begin at 39 °C. By default, at or above 40 °C, the player takes damage every 2 seconds by default, rising steeply near 41 °C. Shade and water help you cool down.

Hunger and thirst
Hot weather can increase thirst consumption by up to 61% due to heat, humidity and direct sunlight. Cool weather increases hunger, especially when wet, by up to 18%. Severe heat can reduce hunger consumption by up to 8%. Weather consumption factors can be disabled under Survival settings, independently of hunger and thirst duration multipliers.

10-day forecast
By default, Weather Forecast unlocks at Survival level 2. The notebook (T) shows today and the next 10 in-game days. Its unlock level and forecast duration can be changed under Survival - Ability balance. Future temperature and humidity are estimates for clear skies because upcoming rainfall is not known.

Settings
Under Survival, adjust damage, movement penalties, heat/cold thresholds and nausea intensity separately.

Planned - not yet available

custominfo-shortdesc-6: Train stamina and breath-holding, escape drowning
custominfo-details-6:
Water stamina
Stamina drains while in water and regenerates on land. When it runs out, the player begins to sink.

Stamina training
Swim actively to accumulate training time. Progress carries over between swims. Each level increases your time on water, but the next level needs more training. The home page shows your maximum seconds, training progress and level (out of 10).

Lung capacity
Stay underwater while you still have oxygen to train your lungs. Training time accumulates across dives. Each level increases oxygen capacity, slightly reduces its consumption, and raises the next training requirement. The home page shows breath-holding seconds, training progress and level (out of 10). Oxygen tanks can add more air.

Last chance
If your stamina runs out and you start sinking, quickly press Space (the Jump action) three times, within 1.6 seconds. You will surge upward briefly. You can make up to three surges per exhaustion. To regain your surges, stay out of water for at least 4 seconds and restore at least 35% stamina. The last chance does not restore oxygen or prevent drowning by itself.

Settings
Starting stamina, oxygen capacity, level bonuses and training requirements can be adjusted in Survival settings
